description: VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL Tucked away in the thick forest region of Virdi village, near Chorla Ghat, Vazra Sakla Waterfall is one of Goa’s most spectacular and lesser-known waterfalls. Falling gracefully from a height of over 140 meters, the twin streams of Vazra Sakla cut through lush greenery and untouched forest, creating a picture-perfect scene that looks straight out of a dream. This is a hidden paradise for nature lovers, trekkers, and photographers looking to explore Goa beyond its beaches. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL WHERE IT IS LOCATED Vazra Sakla Waterfall is located in Virdi, a remote village situated in the Chorla Ghat region, which lies at the tri-junction of Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra. The area is part of the Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Surrounded by thick jungles and biodiversity, this location remains unexplored by mass tourism, making it a peaceful and raw natural spot. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL BEST TIME TO VISIT The best time to visit Vazra Sakla is during the monsoon season (June to September) when the waterfall is in full force, and the surroundings are lush green. The forest comes alive with mist, birdsong, and flowing streams. However, trekking during monsoon can be slippery and tricky—post-monsoon (October to November) is ideal for safer, clearer treks. 🗓 Best Time: June to November 📍 Location: Virdi Village, Chorla Ghat, Goa VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL TREKKING EXPERIENCE AND DIFFICULTY LEVEL The trek to Vazra Sakla Waterfall is moderately difficult and suitable for those with good fitness levels. The trail is adventurous, passing through narrow paths, fallen trees, and uneven terrain. The journey might be tough, but the sight of the powerful twin falls at the end is truly rewarding. If you enjoy forest trails and love a quiet moment in nature, this waterfall will fill your heart with joy. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL WHAT TO CARRY FOR THE TREK Here’s what you should carry for your trek to Vazra Sakla Waterfall: ✅ Good grip trekking shoes ✅ 2 liters of drinking water ✅ Poncho or raincoat (in monsoon) ✅ Insect repellent and leech socks ✅ Energy bars/snacks ✅ First aid kit ✅ Camera/phone for photos (optional but worth it!) VAZRA SAKLA Vazra Sakla is a hidden gem located near Virdi village in the Chorla Ghat region. Tucked away in the dense forests at the intersection of Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra, this waterfall is known for its twin vertical drops and misty cliffs, offering a raw and untouched nature experience. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL PHOTOS If you're a fan of scenic photography, Vazra Sakla Waterfall won’t disappoint. The high twin waterfalls cascading down mossy cliffs surrounded by lush greenery create a perfect frame. Many trekkers and nature lovers share their stunning Vazra Sakla waterfall photos online, especially during monsoon. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL LOCATION The Vazra Sakla Waterfall is located in Virdi, a remote forest village in Chorla Ghat near the Goa-Karnataka-Maharashtra border. The location is rich in biodiversity and offers a refreshing escape from the city. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL TREK The Vazra Sakla waterfall trek is an adventurous trail that runs through thick forests, muddy slopes, and river streams. The trek distance is roughly 4 to 5 km one way, and it's moderately difficult, recommended for experienced trekkers or those with a local guide. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL GOA Though technically on the border, Vazra Sakla is considered part of Goa’s hidden waterfalls due to its proximity. It is often explored by Goan nature groups and is one of the most offbeat natural attractions in the region. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL KARNATAKA Due to its location near Khanapur and Belgaum in Karnataka, many travelers from Karnataka also consider this a Karnataka-side waterfall. The access roads from the Karnataka side are also commonly used to reach the site. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL DIRECTIONS To reach Vazra Sakla, you must drive towards Virdi village via Chorla Ghat, then begin the forest trek. There are no official signboards, so using Google Maps to reach Virdi is helpful, but the trek path should be taken with a local guide to avoid getting lost. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALLS SADA PHOTOS People often confuse Vazra Sakla with nearby Sada Waterfalls, which also features dramatic cliffs. You’ll find Vazra Sakla waterfalls Sada photos tagged online under both names due to their close distance and similar appearance. However, they are distinct waterfalls. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL MAPS You can locate Vazra Sakla Waterfall on Google Maps by searching “Virdi Waterfall” or “Vazra Sakla Waterfalls”. However, since it’s deep inside forest terrain, maps won’t show the exact trekking route. Offline maps or GPS navigation help only till Virdi village. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL TREK DISTANCE The trek to Vazra Sakla Waterfall is about 4 to 5 km one way, and takes 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on your pace and weather conditions. During the monsoon, the trek becomes slippery and adventurous. Good shoes and water bottles are a must. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALLS These twin waterfalls gush down vertically from a high cliff and are most spectacular during the monsoon season (June–September). Surrounded by untouched forest and mist, Vazra Sakla waterfalls offer a quiet, peaceful escape from crowded tourist spots. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL DISTANCE From Panaji (Goa) – approx. 70 km From Belgaum (Karnataka) – approx. 50 km From Mapusa (Goa) – approx. 55–60 km Traveling early in the day is advised, especially if you plan to complete the trek before dark. VAZRA SAKLA FALLS Often referred to as “Vazra Sakla Falls” by locals, this destination is still untouched by mass tourism. The name itself means “lightning rock” in Marathi/Konkani—fitting for the powerful and tall twin streams falling side by side with thunderous sound. VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL 🏞️ SADA WATERFALL Located near the Goa–Karnataka border, Sada Waterfall is another hidden gem surrounded by forest trails, massive rock formations, and freshwater streams. It also has a nearby fort ruin, making it ideal for history lovers. 🐾 MHADEI WILDLIFE SANCTUARY One of Goa’s richest biodiversity zones, Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary is home to tigers, black panthers, rare birds, and glowing mushrooms during monsoon. Perfect for nature walks, wildlife sightings, and eco-tourism. 📸 CHORLA GHAT VIEW POINT Just a short drive from Virdi, this view point offers breathtaking views of the Western Ghats, valleys, and mist-covered hills—especially magical during early mornings and monsoons. 🏡 VALPOI VILLAGE A calm and picturesque Goan village, Valpoi is great for experiencing local Goan culture, small cafes, homestays, and markets. It’s also the gateway to many trekking routes in the northern Western Ghats. 🏞️ ANJUNEM DAM Located a bit further, this dam is set amidst thick forest areas and has picnic-friendly zones. The monsoon view is stunning with overflowing catchment areas and cloud-kissed hills. 🧭 HOW TO REACH VAZRA SAKLA WATERFALL Vazra Sakla is nestled deep in the forests of Virdi village, close to Chorla Ghat, where the borders of Goa, Karnataka, and Maharashtra meet. Since it’s an offbeat location, reaching it involves both road travel and trekking. 🚗 BY ROAD: -From Panaji, Goa: - Distance – approx. 60–70 km - Route – Panaji → Ponda → Sanquelim → Chorla Ghat →Virdi - Travel time – Around 2.5 to 3 hours -From Belgaum, Karnataka: - Distance – approx. 50 km - Route – Belgaum → Khanapur → Chorla Ghat → Virdi - Travel time – Around 2 hours -From Mapusa, Goa: - Distance – approx. 55–60 km - Route – Mapusa → Assonora → Bicholim → Chorla Ghat → Virdi - Travel time – Around 2 to 2.5 hours 🛵 BY TWO-WHEELER OR PRIVATE VEHICLE: The best way to reach is via a private vehicle or hired cab. The roads are narrow and patchy near Virdi, so drive carefully, especially during the monsoon. 🚶 TREKKING ROUTE: From Virdi village, a trek of 4–5 km is required through dense forest and rocky terrain. -Duration: 1.5 to 2 hours (one way) -Difficulty: Moderate -Guide: Highly recommended due to unmarked forest trails ❗ TIPS: -No public transport goes directly to Vazra Sakla. -Mobile network is patchy in the forest—download maps in advance. -Start your trek early in the morning to return before sunset.
